how_claude_should_query_without_chrome.read_only_sql_introspection: Use the Supabase Management API: POST https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/llktvzbbfadmnhfjatrh/database/query with header Authorization: Bearer <PAT> and body {"query": "..."} -- runs arbitrary SQL (including information_schema, pg_catalog, trigger/function definitions) via a single curl/fetch call from Bash. No browser needed. THIS IS THE FIX for the slowness this session hit repeatedly hammering the SQL Editor via Claude in Chrome.
how_claude_should_query_without_chrome.pat_needed: A Supabase Personal Access Token (format sbp_...), generated at supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens. Naoelle has provided one before (described as 'never expires') but it is NEVER persisted to disk or memory by design -- must be re-supplied per session, ideally by Naoelle setting it as a permanent Windows/PowerShell environment variable (e.g. SUPABASE_MANAGEMENT_PAT) so it's just always in the shell env without needing to paste it into chat each time.
how_claude_should_query_without_chrome.read_via_postgrest_alternative: For simple table reads (no joins/introspection needed), the anon key (public, embedded in the frontend bundle already, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in .env.local) works fine against public.* tables with RLS allowing `authenticated_all` -- but anon role may be blocked by RLS depending on policy, so the Management API PAT route is more reliable for ad-hoc diagnostics.
how_claude_should_query_without_chrome.writes_ddl_dml: NEVER executed by Claude directly, ever -- this is a hard standing rule (see feedback_db_changes_via_michel memory). Claude writes the SQL or the Node script; Naoelle (or Michel) runs it herself, either by pasting SQL into the SQL Editor UI or running a Node script locally with $env:SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set. This rule is about who executes, not a technical limitation -- do not work around it even if a faster path exists.

schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.profils.id: equals auth.users.id (no FK constraint enforced at the DB level, but the app code and the handle_new_user trigger both assume this equality -- confirmed via information_schema, profils.id's only constraint is its own PRIMARY KEY, no FK to auth.users)
schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.auth_user_creation_trigger: AFTER INSERT trigger `on_auth_user_created` on auth.users calls public.handle_new_user(). On any new auth.users row it: (1) looks up public.profils_autorises by matching email to get prenom/nom/poste_id/role_acces_id, (2) creates the public.profils row (id=new.id) if missing, (3) links to the 'KIWEE_FR' organisation, (4) assigns role_acces (from profils_autorises, or defaults to 'CONSEILLER' if none pre-set), (5) assigns poste only if profils_autorises had one set. Full function body was pulled via pg_get_functiondef and is in the session transcript of 2026-07-30 if needed again.
schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.profils_autorises_mechanism: This is the pre-authorization allowlist (email, prenom, nom, poste_id, role_acces_id) already wired into the Administration UI (src/lib/data/roles.ts: useProfilsAutorises/useAddProfilAutorise/useUpdateProfilAutorisePosteRole/useRemoveProfilAutorise). To create a real user account WITHOUT them clicking a magic-link email first: (a) ensure a profils_autorises row exists for their email with the right poste_id/role_acces_id, (b) call the Supabase Auth Admin API POST {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users with body {email, email_confirm:true} using the service_role key -- the trigger fires immediately and creates a fully-formed profils row. They can still log in later via the normal magic-link flow; it will authenticate into this same pre-created account.
schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.interactions_table_pagination_bug_fixed_: fetchInteractions() in src/lib/data/interactions.ts had no .range()/.limit(), so PostgREST's default 1000-row cap silently truncated the table to only the 1000 globally-most-recent rows once the Salesforce migration pushed it past ~16900 rows -- any account whose most recent interaction was older than that global cutoff showed an empty activity feed. Fixed with a paginated fetch (4-at-a-time parallel + retries, see git log 'Limite la concurrence du fetch pagine des interactions'). If any OTHER table's useX() hook is later found silently empty despite real data existing, check first whether that table has grown past 1000 rows and whether its fetch function has pagination -- this exact bug class can recur.
schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.compte_id_backfill_bug_fixed_2026-07-30: fix_interactions.js/import_emails.js/add_molinier.js only set interactions.compte_id when the Salesforce WhatId/RelatedToId literally pointed at the Account (prefix 001) -- Tasks/Emails linked to an Opportunity/Contract/nothing left compte_id NULL even though the contact (and therefore the compte) was always resolvable. Fixed in the migration scripts (always fall back to the contact's own compte_id) AND backfilled once in production via a one-off UPDATE (see chat history 2026-07-30 for the exact statement). 6048/16913 rows were affected before the fix.
schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.layout_bug_fixed_2026-07-30: CompteDetail.tsx's 3-column grid and the ActivityFeed component were missing `min-h-0` on flex/grid children -- a classic Tailwind/flexbox gotcha where a flex child grows to fit all its content instead of respecting the parent's bounded height, so `overflow-y-auto` never had anything to actually scroll. Invisible with small demo datasets, became visible once real accounts had 200+ interactions. If a future 'this panel doesn't scroll' report comes in anywhere else in the app, check for the same missing min-h-0 pattern first.
schema_facts_confirmed_2026-07-30.rls_policy_pattern: All tables use a blanket `authenticated_all` policy (for all to authenticated using (true) with check (true)) -- RLS is a coarse authenticated-vs-not gate only; the REAL visibility restriction (who sees which comptes) lives in application code via src/lib/data/visibility.ts (fetchComptesVisibles/fetchSitesVisiblesIds), driven by the profils_comptes table. Do not assume a table is unreadable just because RLS is enabled -- check for a missing authenticated_all policy specifically (this has been a recurring real bug, see kiwee_os_project memory for the audit history).

standing_process_rules: Never execute DDL/DML directly against production -- write the SQL or script, Naoelle (or Michel) runs it. This is a deliberate process choice, not a technical limitation; don't route around it even when a faster path exists.

Never assume a fact about data/schema state -- always verify with a targeted, specific query before asserting something exists, is empty, or has a certain count. A long aggregate query can silently truncate; prefer `select count(*) from x where y` over trusting a big joined dump.
Commit and push directly to master without asking for confirmation each time, for every code change (but never force-push, never amend published commits, never skip hooks).
After editing any sf_import/*.js script, copy it to Desktop\import-pilote-kimatch\ before telling Naoelle to run it -- the execution copy and the source copy have drifted before.

Before designating any account as a 'known-good reference' to validate an approach, verify it's actually inside whatever dataset/batch is being discussed -- Cabinet Molinier looked like a valid reference account but wasn't even in the imported pilot batch.
